es: Responder a un oyente que malinterpretó un segmento: resumir, corregir con un ejemplo, conceder un punto y proponer un tema nuevo.

vocabulary.es: dejar las cosas claras, aclarar los hechos

teaching.en: Thank you for your message: there seems to be a misunderstanding, so I would like to set the record straight before we move on.
teaching.es: Gracias por tu mensaje: parece haber un malentendido, así que quiero dejar las cosas claras antes de seguir.
teaching.explanationEs: There seems to be a misunderstanding nombra el problema con cortesía; set the record straight anuncia la corrección.
segments: Thank you for your message: there seems to be a misunderstanding, so
I would like to set the record straight before we move on.
teaching.audioText: Thank you for your message: there seems to be a misunderstanding, so I would like to set the record straight before we move on.

teaching.en: What the guest actually said was that recordings can help, not that they replace the classroom, and in fact she warned against relying on them alone.
teaching.es: Lo que la invitada dijo en realidad fue que las grabaciones pueden ayudar, no que sustituyan al aula, y de hecho advirtió contra depender solo de ellas.
teaching.explanationEs: What … actually said was that… corrige con precisión; in fact añade un dato que refuerza la corrección.
segments: What the guest actually said was that recordings can help, not that they
replace the classroom, and in fact she warned against relying on them alone.
teaching.audioText: What the guest actually said was that recordings can help, not that they replace the classroom, and in fact she warned against relying on them alone.

teaching.en: To be fair, the listener is right about one thing: it is easy to oversimplify a long debate, and a short summary can misrepresent a speaker's view.
teaching.es: Para ser justos, el oyente tiene razón en una cosa: es fácil simplificar en exceso un debate largo, y un resumen corto puede tergiversar la opinión de un hablante.
teaching.explanationEs: To be fair concede un punto antes de seguir; oversimplify y misrepresent nombran dos formas de deformar lo dicho.
segments: To be fair, the listener is right about one thing: it is easy to
oversimplify a long debate, and a short summary can misrepresent a speaker's view.
teaching.audioText: To be fair, the listener is right about one thing: it is easy to oversimplify a long debate, and a short summary can misrepresent a speaker's view.

teaching.en: I would like to correct one detail and clarify the host's position, because her caution was not the same as a rejection.
teaching.es: Quisiera corregir un detalle y aclarar la postura de la presentadora, porque su cautela no equivalía a un rechazo.
teaching.explanationEs: Correct corrige un dato; clarify aclara algo que se entendió a medias.
segments: I would like to correct one detail and clarify the host's
position, because her caution was not the same as a rejection.
teaching.audioText: I would like to correct one detail and clarify the host's position, because her caution was not the same as a rejection.

teaching.en: We will take on board your criticism, and we propose a segment about homework next week, because many listeners have asked for it.
teaching.es: Tendremos en cuenta tu crítica, y proponemos un segmento sobre los deberes la semana próxima, porque muchos oyentes lo han pedido.
teaching.explanationEs: Take on board = asumir una crítica sin ponerse a la defensiva; propose + nombre introduce el tema nuevo y su razón.
segments: We will take on board your criticism, and we propose a segment
about homework next week, because many listeners have asked for it.
teaching.audioText: We will take on board your criticism, and we propose a segment about homework next week, because many listeners have asked for it.

teaching.en: In fact, the best replies thank the listener first, correct the idea with an example and only then offer a concession.
teaching.es: De hecho, las mejores respuestas agradecen primero al oyente, corrigen la idea con un ejemplo y solo después ofrecen una concesión.
teaching.explanationEs: El orden importa: agradecer, corregir la idea (no a la persona), conceder y proponer.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que corrige el malentendido con más precisión.

choices.text: What I actually said was that late phone use can affect concentration, not that it guarantees bad marks.
What I actually said was that every student who uses a phone at night will get bad marks.
In fact, I said that late phone use has no effect on concentration at all.

feedback.es: Corrige con la estructura «what … actually said was that… not that…»: fija lo que sí se dijo y descarta la versión exagerada.

hint.es: Busca la frase que niega la versión del oyente sin inventar otra.

origin.text: Listener: You said that every student who uses a phone at night will get bad marks. Host: I am sorry, but that is not what happened in the segment.

prompt.es: Completa: «Parece haber un malentendido sobre lo que dijo en realidad.»

feedback.es: There seems to be a misunderstanding es la fórmula cortés para nombrar el problema sin acusar al oyente.

origin.text: The listener thinks that the guest wants to ban every phone. There seems to be a ___ about what she actually said.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Para ser justos, tienes razón en una cosa.»

answer.text: To be fair, you are right about one thing

feedback.es: To be fair abre la concesión y va seguido de lo que el oyente sí tiene de razón.

hint.es: La concesión empieza con to be fair.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de una respuesta con el movimiento que realiza.

pairs: There seems to be a misunderstanding.
What she actually said was that recordings can help.
To be fair, you are right about the cost.
Next week, I propose a segment on homework.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta recorre cuatro movimientos: nombrar, corregir, conceder y proponer.

prompt.es: ¿Qué problema tiene este borrador de respuesta a un oyente?

choices.text: It concedes too many points and forgets to correct the error.
It corrects the idea but attacks the listener instead of clarifying.
It is very formal and never mentions the disagreement.

feedback.es: Corrige el dato, pero lo hace culpando al oyente («you clearly did not listen»): falta tacto y falta aclarar qué se dijo.

origin.text: Draft reply: You clearly did not listen to the segment. The guest never said that. Please check the facts before you write to us again.

prompt.es: Escribe en inglés: «Quiero aclarar un detalle antes de continuar.»

answer.text: I would like to clarify one detail before we move on.
accepted: I would like to clarify one detail before we move on.
I want to clarify one detail before we move on.
Let me clarify one detail before we move on.

feedback.es: Clarify + un detalle aclara lo que se entendió mal; before we move on anuncia que después se cambia de asunto.

origin.text: Quieres aclarar un detalle antes de pasar al siguiente tema.

prompt.es: Escucha a la presentadora y elige qué hace con «to be fair».

choices.text: She apologises and takes back what the guest said.
She moves on to the topic of next week's show.
She concedes one point while keeping her correction.

feedback.es: Reconoce que los resultados importan para acceder a una plaza, pero mantiene su corrección sobre lo que dijo el invitado.

origin.audio: The host reads out a message from a listener who believes that the guest wants to cancel every test. She pauses and answers: thank you, but there seems to be a misunderstanding. What the guest actually said was that one big test should not decide everything, not that tests are useless. To be fair, you are right that marks matter when students apply for a place. I would like to come back to that point next week.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué da a entender la presentadora sobre el invitado.

choices.text: That his view was more careful than the listener thought.
That his view was wrong and the listener was right.
That his view was the same as the host's opinion.

feedback.es: Dice que no defiende que los exámenes sean inútiles, sino que uno solo no debe decidirlo todo: su postura era más matizada.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quiero dejar las cosas claras: solo pidió normas claras en clase.»

feedback.es: Set the record straight es la colocación para aclarar los hechos cuando alguien los ha entendido mal.

origin.text: A listener wrote that the guest wanted to ban every phone. I would like to set the record ___: she only asked for clear rules in class.

prompt.es: Responde al oyente: malentendido, corrección, concesión y tema nuevo.

answer.text: Hello, and thank you for your message. There seems to be a misunderstanding, and I would like to set the record straight. What Dr Patel actually said was that recordings help students who miss a class, not that nobody needs to come to school. In fact, she acknowledged that attendance may fall, and she admitted that teachers may feel watched, so she suggested recording only the main lessons. To be fair, you are right about one thing: the host was sceptical, and he raised a concern about exactly this point. We will take on board your criticism, because it is easy to oversimplify a long debate. Overall, both speakers called the idea a reasonable compromise. By the way, I propose a segment about homework next week, since several listeners have asked for it. Thank you for listening.
accepted: Hello, and thank you for your message. There seems to be a misunderstanding, and I would like to set the record straight. What Dr Patel actually said was that recordings help students who miss a class, not that nobody needs to come to school. In fact, she acknowledged that attendance may fall, and she admitted that teachers may feel watched, so she suggested recording only the main lessons. To be fair, you are right about one thing: the host was sceptical, and he raised a concern about exactly this point. We will take on board your criticism, because it is easy to oversimplify a long debate. Overall, both speakers called the idea a reasonable compromise. By the way, I propose a segment about homework next week, since several listeners have asked for it. Thank you for listening.

Thanks for writing to us. I think there is a misunderstanding here. The guest never said that students do not need to come to school. In fact, she admitted that attendance could fall, she acknowledged that teachers may feel watched, and she suggested recording only the main lessons. You are right about one thing, though: the host sounded sceptical and he said the same. We will take on board your comment, because a short summary can easily misrepresent a speaker's view. To sum up, the guest supports recordings with clear limits. As for next week, I propose a segment about homework, because you and other listeners have asked for it. Thank you for listening.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta agradece, nombra el malentendido, corrige con verbos de habla exactos, concede un punto y propone un tema nuevo con una razón.

origin.text:
Segment notes: The guest maintains that recordings help students who miss a class. She acknowledges that attendance may fall, admits that teachers may feel watched, and suggests recording only the main lessons. The host is sceptical but calls the idea a reasonable compromise.
Listener message: Hi! I listened to your segment on recording lessons. Dr Patel said that students never need to come to school if every lesson is online, and that teachers have nothing to worry about. That seems too simple to me! By the way, could you cover homework next week?

prompt.es: Lee el segundo correo de la oyente. ¿Qué actitud muestra ahora?

choices.text: She gives up her opinion and praises the guest.
She accepts the correction while keeping her own opinion.
She rejects the correction and repeats her first claim.

feedback.es: Acepta que entendió mal a la invitada, pero mantiene su opinión sobre las aulas vacías: corrección aceptada, postura intacta.

origin.text: Listener's second email: Thanks for clearing that up. I still think that recordings will empty our classrooms, but I accept that I understood Dr Patel badly. Please keep covering this subject.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tendremos en cuenta tu crítica y propondremos un tema nuevo.»

answer.text: We will take on board your criticism and propose a new topic

feedback.es: Take on board + criticism asume la crítica; después, propose introduce la mejora concreta.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un resumen breve puede tergiversar la opinión de un hablante.»

feedback.es: Misrepresent es deformar lo que alguien dijo, por ejemplo al omitir las condiciones de su postura.

origin.text: A very short summary can easily ___ a speaker's view when it leaves out the conditions he attached to it.
